title: Muscle fatigue as a falling median frequency: the myoelectric signature on real sustained-contraction EMG

dataset.name: Multi-channel Surface EMG Dataset for Fatigue analysis
dataset.record: 15 healthy subjects, 8-channel surface EMG @ 200 Hz, 6 kg load, elbow 90 deg, 120 s sustained isometric contraction
dataset.citation: Ebied A, Awadallah AM, Abbass MA, El-Sharkawy Y. Upper Limb Muscle Fatigue Analysis Using Multi-channel Surface EMG. 2020 NILES, pp. 423-427. doi:10.1109/NILES50944.2020.9257909. Dataset: doi:10.5281/zenodo.5189275 (CC-BY-4.0).

proposition: On real 120 s sustained-contraction surface EMG, the ecosystem recovers the classic myoelectric fatigue signature: the power-spectrum median frequency (MDF) falls over the hold (cohort mean final/initial MDF ratio 0.918, a 8.2% drop, from 63.3 Hz to 58.2 Hz), with the decline present in 14 of 15 subjects.

claims.statement: subjects whose median frequency declines (fatigue index < 1), of 15
cohort mean fatigue index (final / initial MDF)
cohort mean MDF percent change over the hold

validation.reference: The established myoelectric-fatigue law — a monotonic decline of the EMG spectrum's median frequency under sustained contraction (De Luca 1984) — and the dataset's own fatiguing protocol (6 kg, 120 s hold)
validation.data: REAL — Ebied et al. 2021 (Zenodo 5189275), 15 healthy subjects, 8-channel sEMG @ 200 Hz
validation.note: Aggregate acceptance: the cohort mean fatigue index is < 1 (0.918) and the fatigue direction holds in >= 90% of subjects (14/15). The one exception (sub4, index 1.001) is reported, not dropped. The absolute MDF values (~55-70 Hz) are shaped by the acquisition — 200 Hz sampling (100 Hz Nyquist) with a 50 Hz notch sitting inside the EMG band — so they are not universal constants; the reproducible finding is the within-recording decline, which a fixed notch cannot manufacture.

open_questions.q: One subject (sub4) shows essentially no MDF decline (fatigue index 1.001) under this 6 kg / 120 s load; whether that reflects lower relative effort, better fatigue resistance, or electrode placement is not identifiable from this recording alone. Documented, not escalated.
